summary.text: A 14-year-old patient presented to the hospital after a fall from height during recreational activity, without loss of consciousness, with twisting trauma of the left ankle. Examination showed pain and functional impairment of the affected limb, palpable distal pulses, good capillary filling and no motor or sensory deficit. Radiographs revealed a Tillaux fracture of the distal left tibia with a confirmed Salter-Harris type IV injury and a posterior malleolus fracture on the lateral view.

The patient was immediately immobilized with a splint and tomographic images were requested to plan surgery. Surgery was closed reduction percutaneous fixation under fluoroscopic guidance with traction and internal rotation, with a cannulated screw and washer placed across the epiphysis. The patient left the operating room in a splint for the first week and remained non-weight-bearing for four weeks while performing isometric exercises.

At follow-up the patient had improved clinical status and favorable healing on X-rays. Kinesic rehabilitation was not suggested; activities and isometric exercises were permitted and regular follow-up over three months was advised. At the two-month visit the patient used crutches; at three months radiographs showed consolidation and the patient entered unaided, without pain, with normal gait, good ankle range of motion and strength and no swelling. The AOFAS score was 92 points at 75 days and 100 points at 90 days after surgery.
